prediction_question: For a building-code violation case docketed with the Chicago Department of Administrative Hearings, will the hearing officer ultimately find the respondent liable?
prediction_time: At docketing, before the hearing date. Permitted features are the violation, the property and the docket metadata. case_disposition, imposed_fine, admin_costs and last_modified_date are outcomes and excluded.
target_definition: Binary: case_disposition == 'Liable' versus 'Not Liable'. Cases disposed as Non-Suit, Default, Continuance, Adjudication Performance / Other, Dismissed Without Prejudice and Judgment Vacated are excluded from the binary task and reported separately as a multi-class follow-up.

construction_script: candidates/chicago-doah-adjudication/build.py (stdlib only, runs on a worker; 18 anonymous Socrata requests - one count(*) probe and 17 pages of 50,000 rows ordered by :id; --built-at pins meta.json's timestamp so a rebuild is byte-comparable)

construction_output.note: Case-level temporal splits over the case's earliest recorded violation date. Row counts and positive rates were measured over the shipped CSVs (the bytes covered by SHA256SUMS) after collection from the worker. The positive rate rises across windows because the City republishes this dataset continuously and older dockets are progressively cleaned up; it is a property of the source, not of the construction.

split_strategy: Temporal by the case's earliest recorded violation (notice) date, taken over cases and never over the source's charge rows: train 2008-01-01..2018-01-01, eval 2018-01-01..2022-01-01, holdout 2022-01-01..2026-09-01. No random split; the builder asserts that no docket_number spans two files.

measurements.deviation_note: Single observations, not distributions. Extraction cost is two measurements - one local, one on a worker - that agreed to within a second on wall clock and produced byte-identical artifacts.

jobs: chicago-001 (gate passed, artifact superseded: it shipped hearing_date and a derived days_to_hearing feature, which is post-hoc leakage - the City documents hearing_date as the date of the most recent hearing, so on a decided case it is the hearing at which the disposition was recorded. days_to_hearing separates the classes on its own, single-column AUC 0.84 over the case rows. Defect found by inspection, not by the gate.)
chicago-002 (same builder, re-run: produced identical source_rows_sha256 and case_table_sha256, so the build was shown deterministic on a second worker. Superseded with chicago-001 by the same fix.)
chicago-003 (released artifact: hearing_date not read at all, split re-keyed to violation_date, window enforced on the case date; gate 1.3.0 passed 32 checks, 0 failed.)
chicago-baseline-001 (one baseline through the runner's own train.py/validate.sh, unmodified and hash-verified: eval AUC 0.6915 from both, contract OK.)
chicago-consumer-001 (fresh environment with no factory access: run.sh exit 0, digests and sha256sum -c OK, qualification PASSED, baseline eval AUC 0.6915.)

chicago-hf-001 (Hugging Face publish: all five files uploaded and re-hashed at the published revision, but the job's own loading check failed - the documented load returned splits train/test and reported eval and holdout missing, because the card then declared no configs block. The card was fixed to declare the manifest's three splits and the documented path was re-verified anonymously at revision v2026.09: train 47414 / eval 3436 / holdout 2913 rows, 11 columns, label values Liable / Not Liable, matching the manifest. Worker destroyed.)

novelty_check.theirs: The raw dataset is already mirrored on Kaggle and catalogued on Data.gov, so access is not the contribution. Adjacent literature exists: models that predict building-code compliance to target inspections, housing-code violation prediction from integrated city data, and a 2026 preprint on predicting building-code waiver outcomes. None of them package adjudication outcomes as a frozen, split, leakage-gated task.
novelty_check.ours: A frozen extract of Chicago Ordinance Violations with recorded checksums; a binary outcome label (Liable vs Not Liable) at case level rather than row level; a split by docket_number so a case cannot leak across periods; a natural future holdout of hearings not yet ruled; and a leakage-gated runner contract around all of it. No package of this task exists.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
